A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UnifiedReward-Think. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training-stage ablations, and qualitative reward-model outputs in Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–8.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds rejection-sampling, backbone, and distillation-source experiments in Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: Section 3.4.2 revises the stated GRPO objective by placing the advantage inside both branches of the minimum, changing its behavior for negative advantages. Whether the implementation changed is unstated. The three-stage pipeline remains intact; the scoring strategy emphasized in new Section 3.5 already appears in v1 Appendix A and its prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate image/video generation and understanding reward tasks using the same dataset coverage. ImageGen-CoT-Reward-5K names the previously described cold-start collection. The added experiments vary training stages, backbones, and distillation sources without introducing new tasks or evaluation domains.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their external comparator sets. New Tables 5–7 add comparisons with a no-rejection-sampling variant and Qwen backbone/distillation variants, providing limited additional comparison methods within the proposed method family.

E3.justification: v2 adds experiments omitting rejection sampling, using Qwen2.5-VL-7B as backbone, and distilling from Qwen2.5-VL-72B. Appendix D reports cold-start sampling from HPD, EvalMuse, and OIP, whereas v1 Section 4.1 specifies four image-generation datasets. This changes the reported sourcing protocol without establishing that existing experiments were rerun; retained evaluation metrics and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's progressive training-stage and GRPO-without-CoT ablations, v2 adds a direct rejection-sampling omission control, robustness testing on another backbone, and an alternative distillation-teacher experiment. Tables 5–7 substantially broaden analysis of stage necessity and dependence on model and teacher choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The retained eight-response GRPO sampling setting and reward standardization describe the algorithm, not uncertainty estimation for experimental results.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values. Tables 5–7 add substantive findings: omitting rejection sampling yields 70.4 versus 73.8 VLReward overall accuracy; the Qwen backbone scores 76.6/84.0 on GenAI image/video versus 72.5/82.3 for LLaVA; alternative-teacher results show mixed, relatively small differences. These are newly reported configuration comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The GRPO surrogate changes from min(ratio, clipped ratio) multiplied by advantage to min(ratio multiplied by advantage, clipped ratio multiplied by advantage). These expressions differ for negative advantages, making this a mathematical correction rather than equivalent notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of a unified multimodal CoT reward model, improved explicit reward reasoning, and improved direct responses through implicit reasoning. The newly emphasized multidimensional scoring strategy was already described in v1; the additional experiments support retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking cross-task transfer to unified input/output structure, interpreting alternative-teacher results through cold start's format-learning role, and motivating exclusion of ties for discriminative ranking. It also explains the format reward's protective role. Existing inference-cost and RL-capacity limitations largely move into Section 5.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents selecting 10K candidate samples and filtering them to 5K cold-start examples. Table 6 explicitly identifies the original LLaVA-OneVision-7B backbone. Training hyperparameters and hardware move unchanged from v1 Appendix B.2 to v2 Section 4.1; no new code or dataset access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Pref-GRPO, Wang et al. 2025a, to the introduction and references while retaining the main research positioning. Its two Bai et al. entries duplicate the Qwen2.5-VL report already cited in v1 and do not represent two new works.

P1.justification: v2 expands selected introduction and method explanations, adds Section 3.5, moves training details and limitations into the main text, and reorganizes the appendices around new analyses. Citation formatting, heading capitalization, author footnotes, and venue text change, but most existing prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact appendix tables, adjusts captions and table emphasis, and relocates figures and tables through text reflow. Figures 1–8 retain their substantive visual content. These are localized display and layout changes rather than a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–7 strengthen evidence for rejection sampling and robustness to backbone and teacher choices. The corrected GRPO expression and additional cold-start construction details also improve technical clarity. These gains are limited: headline results remain unchanged, uncertainty estimates are still absent, and the PDFs do not explain whether revised objective and cold-start sourcing descriptions reflect implementation changes or reporting corrections.
